Symptoms worsen after exertion and improve with rest; there is no sensory loss or fever. Strength is mildly reduced during symptoms but returns toward baseline after rest. The patient received an influenza vaccine 4 months ago. A membrane recording shows resting potassium conductance is much greater than resting sodium conductance, and intracellular impermeant anions are preserved. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the electrophysiologic finding?
choices: ATP hydrolysis directly creates all membrane voltage
Calcium influx sets the resting potential
Chloride is the only permeant ion
Potassium efflux leaves behind impermeant intracellular anions
Sodium influx creates the entire negative potential

Glomerular Filtration.caseStem: A 24-year-old man is evaluated in the emergency department for a change in urine output or kidney function. The current episode began 4 hours ago. The medication list, recent fluid intake, and timing of urine collection are reviewed before treatment is started. Cardiopulmonary examination is normal, and the bladder is not distended. Blood pressure is 132/78 mm Hg, mucous membranes are moist, and there is no peripheral edema. The patient takes a daily multivitamin. Glomerular Filtration.caseStem: A 45-year-old man is evaluated in an outpatient clinic for a change in urine output or kidney function. The current episode began 3 days ago. The medication list, recent fluid intake, and timing of urine collection are reviewed before treatment is started. Blood pressure is 132/78 mm Hg, mucous membranes are moist, and there is no peripheral edema. Family history is notable for hypertension in one parent. During water deprivation, epithelial water flux increases rapidly when ADH is present and a transepithelial osmotic gradient is maintained. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the clinical and laboratory findings?
Urine Concentration Mechanism.explanation: NaCl reabsorption without water in the thick ascending limb builds the medullary osmotic gradient.

Blood pressure is 132/78 mm Hg, mucous membranes are moist, and there is no peripheral edema. The patient received an influenza vaccine 4 months ago. Arterial blood gas and serum chemistry are obtained at the same time, allowing the primary disturbance to be distinguished from compensation.

Which of the following body-fluid changes best explains the combined laboratory findings after equilibration?

Decreased ECF volume, increased ICF volume, and decreased osmolality
Decreased hematocrit from plasma volume expansion
Increased ECF volume and decreased ICF volume
Increased ECF volume with unchanged osmolality
Body Volume.explanation: Hypotonic contraction removes more solute than water from the ECF, lowering osmolality and shifting water into cells. ECF volume falls, ICF volume rises, and plasma proteins and hematocrit tend to increase.
choiceExplanations: Incorrect. This predicts the opposite direction of the change supported by the vignette. The stem findings fit Decreased ECF volume, increased ICF volume, and decreased osmolality.

Endocrine & Metabolism.caseStem: A 49-year-old woman is evaluated during a preoperative evaluation after an acute physiologic stressor involving more than one organ system.
